chunks: And from him from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin who said:

I asked the Servant of God (peace be upon him) about the recitation in the Witr prayer, and I said: 'Some have narrated that one recites "Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad" in all three [rak'ahs], and some have narrated that one recites the two Mu'awwidhat (Al-Falaq and An-Nas) in the first two [rak'ahs] and "Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad" in the third.' He said: 'Act according to the Mu'awwidhat and "Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad".'
And the Taslim (salutation of peace) in the two [rak'ahs] of the three rak'ahs is not permissible to omit; what has been narrated indicates this:

key_terms.اَلتَّسْلِيمُ: Taslim (salutation of peace concluding the prayer)
key_terms.اَلْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Surahs of protection (Al-Falaq and An-Nas)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method of recitation and Taslim in the three-rak'ah Witr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* resolves the juristic debate regarding Witr recitations by prescribing a specific sequence: the two Mu'awwidhat in the first two rak'ahs and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the third, reflecting the Shia emphasis on structured devotion. It further clarifies that the Taslim after the second rak'ah is obligatory, distinguishing the Witr prayer's structure from other voluntary prayers. This guidance underscores the practical application of Quranic recitation in daily worship, linking spiritual protection with ritual precision.
